title: West Ham Fall at Portsmouth as Scott Parker's Wait for a Win Goes On
body:
West Ham came away from Portsmouth with nothing [S1]. Scott Parker is still waiting for his first win at West Ham [S1]. That is the detail that stings, because a new manager can survive a bad afternoon but not a long run without a victory.

Elsewhere in the same Championship roundup, Middlesbrough beat Swansea 2-1 to cement their place at the top [S1]. Will Lankshear was back among the goals, claiming his 14th league goal of the season, which makes him the division's leading scorer [S1]. Joseph Opoku had levelled with a driven finish before Lankshear restored the lead in the second half [S1]. Preston also kept their revival going with a 4-0 win over Cardiff [S1].

There is no form table or prediction in the material to lean on, so the honest read is about mood and momentum rather than numbers. The scoreboard shows a side that is still searching for a result it can build on, and the league table around it is moving on.

It was the kind of game that tells you more about character than tactics, and character is what this side now has to prove. Results like this shape a season far more than any press conference ever will.

The Touchline Take: file this one under unfinished business.

evidence.text: The Guardian: Championship roundup: Boro edge Swansea, West Ham lose at Portsmouth. Preston revival continues in 4-0 thrashing of Cardiff. Scott Parker still waiting for first win at Hammers. Will Lankshear was back among the goals as Middlesbrough cemented their position at the top of the Championship with a 2-1 win over Swansea . Lankshear had missed the final two games before the international break because of a hamstring injury, and was only afforded a late substitute appearance in Saturday’s win over Bristol City. Having been restored to the starting lineup at the Riverside, the Championship’s leading scorer claimed his 14th league goal of the season to re-establish his side’s lead in the second half after Joseph Opoku’s driven finish had cancelled out Myles Peart-Harris’ opener.
